questions.q: The SI unit of amount of substance is the ______.
questions.e: One mole contains 6.022 × 10^23 elementary entities (Avogadro's number).

questions.q: Calculate the molar mass of sulphuric acid, H2SO4 (H = 1, S = 32, O = 16).
How many moles of water are present in 36 g of water?
questions.e: Molar mass of H2O = 18 g/mol, so moles = 36/18 = 2 mol.

questions.q: 4 g of NaOH is dissolved in water to make 250 mL of solution. Find its molarity (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1).
questions.e: Moles = 4/40 = 0.1 mol; molarity = 0.1/0.25 L = 0.4 M.

questions.q: A compound contains 40% carbon, 6.67% hydrogen and 53.33% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula?
questions.e: Mole ratio C : H : O = 3.33 : 6.67 : 3.33 = 1 : 2 : 1, giving CH2O.

questions.q: Methane burns in air: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O. Riya burns 16 g of methane completely (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16).
p: (a) How many moles of methane are burnt?
mol
(b) What mass of oxygen is required?
g
(c) What mass of carbon dioxide is formed?
g
questions.e: 16 g CH4 = 1 mol; it needs 2 mol O2 = 64 g and gives 1 mol CO2 = 44 g.

questions.q: The neutron was discovered by ______.
questions.e: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in the shell with n = 3?
questions.e: Maximum electrons in a shell = 2n^2 = 2 × 9 = 18.

questions.q: How many orbitals are present in a subshell with azimuthal quantum number l = 2?
questions.e: Number of orbitals = 2l + 1 = 5 (the five d orbitals).

questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are present in a ground-state iron atom (Z = 26)?
questions.e: Fe is [Ar] 3d6 4s2; by Hund's rule the six d electrons fill as one pair and four singles, giving 4 unpaired electrons.

questions.q: Chlorine (Z = 17) occurs as two isotopes: Cl-35 (75%) and Cl-37 (25%).
p: (a) How many neutrons are there in a Cl-37 atom?
(b) What is the average atomic mass of chlorine?
u
(c) How many electrons does a chloride ion, Cl-, have?
questions.e: Neutrons = 37 − 17 = 20; average mass = 0.75 × 35 + 0.25 × 37 = 35.5 u; Cl- has 17 + 1 = 18 electrons.

questions.q: In Bohr's model, the energy of the electron in the hydrogen atom is En = −13.6/n^2 eV.
p: (a) What is the energy of the electron in the first orbit?
eV
(b) What is its energy in the second orbit?
eV
(c) What is the energy of the photon emitted when the electron jumps from n = 2 to n = 1?
eV
questions.e: E1 = −13.6 eV, E2 = −13.6/4 = −3.4 eV; the photon carries E2 − E1 = 10.2 eV (first Lyman line).

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The modern periodic law states that properties of elements are a periodic function of their ______.
questions.e: Moseley showed atomic number, not atomic mass, is the fundamental property; this is the modern periodic law.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: How many groups are there in the long form of the modern periodic table?
questions.e: The IUPAC long form has 18 vertical columns (groups) and 7 periods.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The most electronegative element in the periodic table is ______.
questions.e: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity (4.0 on the Pauling scale) due to its small size and high nuclear attraction.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: On moving from left to right across a period, the atomic radius generally ______.
questions.e: Nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same shell, so they are pulled closer and the radius decreases.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: An element has the electronic configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5. To which group of the periodic table does it belong?
questions.e: It is a p-block element with 7 valence electrons (ns2 np5), so group = 10 + 7 = 17 (it is chlorine).

questions.q: A bond formed by mutual sharing of electrons between two atoms is called a/an ______ bond.
questions.e: In a covalent bond, each atom contributes electrons to a shared pair, as in H2 or Cl2.

questions.q: According to VSEPR theory, the shape of the methane (CH4) molecule is ______.
questions.e: Four bond pairs and no lone pairs around carbon arrange tetrahedrally with bond angles of 109.5°.

questions.q: What is the H–O–H bond angle in a water molecule?
questions.e: Two lone pairs on oxygen repel the bond pairs more strongly, reducing the angle from 109.5° to 104.5°.

questions.q: According to molecular orbital theory, what is the bond order of the O2 molecule?
questions.e: O2 has 10 bonding and 6 antibonding valence electrons, so bond order = (10 − 6)/2 = 2.

questions.q: What is the hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethyne (HC≡CH)?
questions.e: Each carbon forms two σ bonds and two π bonds, using two sp hybrid orbitals; the molecule is linear.

questions.q: How many sigma (σ) bonds are present in a molecule of but-1-en-3-yne, CH2=CH–C≡CH?
questions.e: There are 4 C–H σ bonds and 3 C–C σ bonds (one in each of C=C, C–C and C≡C), giving 7 σ bonds and 3 π bonds.

questions.q: A property whose value depends only on the state of the system and not on the path followed is called a ______ function.
questions.e: Internal energy, enthalpy and entropy are state functions; heat and work are path functions.

questions.q: An isolated system can exchange neither energy nor ______ with its surroundings.
questions.e: Water in a perfectly insulated, closed thermos flask is an example of an isolated system.

questions.q: For the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g), what is Δng (change in number of moles of gas)?
questions.e: Δng = moles of gaseous products − reactants = 2 − 4 = −2; this is used in ΔH = ΔU + ΔngRT.

questions.q: For a reaction at 300 K, ΔH = −10 kJ/mol and ΔS = +20 J/K/mol. Calculate ΔG in kJ/mol.
questions.e: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = −10 − 300 × 0.020 = −16 kJ/mol, so the reaction is spontaneous.

questions.q: A reaction has ΔH = +30 kJ/mol and ΔS = +100 J/K/mol. Above what temperature does it become spontaneous?
questions.e: At equilibrium ΔG = 0, so T = ΔH/ΔS = 30000/100 = 300 K; above this, TΔS exceeds ΔH.

questions.q: What is the pH of pure water at 298 K?
questions.e: In pure water [H3O+] = 10^-7 M at 298 K, so pH = 7.

questions.q: Find the pH of a 0.01 M HCl solution.
questions.e: HCl is a strong acid, so [H+] = 10^-2 M and pH = −log(10^-2) = 2.

questions.q: By Le Chatelier's principle, adding more reactant to a system at equilibrium shifts the equilibrium in the ______ direction.
questions.e: The system tries to consume the added reactant, so more products are formed.

questions.q: Find the pH of a 0.001 M NaOH solution at 298 K.
For H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), the equilibrium concentrations are [H2] = 0.1 M, [I2] = 0.1 M and [HI] = 0.8 M.
p: (a) Calculate Kc.
(b) What is Δng for this reaction?
(c) What is the value of Kp at the same temperature?

questions.q: Name the conjugate base of water (H2O) in the Bronsted–Lowry sense.
questions.e: Removing a proton from H2O gives OH-, its conjugate base.

questions.q: In terms of electron transfer, oxidation is defined as the loss of ______.
questions.e: Oxidation is loss of electrons and reduction is gain of electrons.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of manganese in KMnO4?
What is the oxidation number of chromium in K2Cr2O7?
What is the average oxidation number of sulphur in sodium thiosulphate, Na2S2O3?
In acidic medium, MnO4- is reduced to Mn2+ and Fe2+ is oxidised to Fe3+. How many moles of KMnO4 are needed to oxidise 5 moles of Fe2+?
questions.e: Each MnO4- gains 5 electrons (Mn +7 → +2) and each Fe2+ loses 1, so 1 mol MnO4- oxidises 5 mol Fe2+.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: Write the IUPAC name of CH3CH2OH.
questions.e: Two carbons (eth-), saturated (-an-) with an –OH group (-ol): ethanol.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: Two miscible liquids with widely different boiling points are separated by simple ______.
questions.e: The lower-boiling liquid vaporises first, is condensed and collected separately.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: What is the hybridisation of the positively charged carbon in a carbocation?
questions.e: The carbocation carbon has three σ bonds and an empty p orbital, so it is sp2 hybridised and trigonal planar.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: The permanent displacement of σ-bond electrons along a carbon chain due to an electronegative atom is called the ______ effect.
questions.e: In the inductive effect, e.g. in CH3CH2Cl, Cl pulls σ electrons and the effect weakens along the chain.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: In Lassaigne's test, the presence of nitrogen is shown by the formation of a ______ colour.
questions.e: Sodium cyanide formed in the fusion gives ferric ferrocyanide, which is Prussian blue.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: On complete combustion, 0.2 g of an organic compound gave 0.44 g of CO2 (C = 12, O = 16).
p: (a) What mass of carbon is present in 0.44 g of CO2?
g
(b) What is the percentage of carbon in the compound?
(c) Nitrogen in such compounds can be estimated by converting it to ammonium sulphate. Name this method.
Kjeldahl|Kjeldahl's|Kjeldahl method|Kjeldahl's method
questions.e: Mass of C = 12/44 × 0.44 = 0.12 g, so %C = 0.12/0.2 × 100 = 60%; Kjeldahl's method converts N to (NH4)2SO4.

questions.q: The simplest alkyne is ______.
questions.e: Ethyne (HC≡CH), commonly called acetylene, has the C≡C triple bond with just two carbons.

questions.q: Addition of HBr to propene giving 2-bromopropane as the major product follows ______ rule.
questions.e: H adds to the carbon with more H atoms via the more stable secondary carbocation, so Br goes to the middle carbon.

questions.q: How many π electrons are present in a benzene ring?
questions.e: Benzene has three C=C double bonds, i.e. 6 delocalised π electrons, satisfying Huckel's (4n + 2) rule with n = 1.

questions.q: Ozonolysis of but-2-ene (CH3CH=CHCH3) followed by Zn/H2O gives two molecules of ______.
questions.e: The C=C bond is cleaved in the middle, each half becoming CH3CHO (ethanal).

questions.q: How many structural (chain) isomers are possible for the alkane C5H12?
questions.e: They are n-pentane, 2-methylbutane (isopentane) and 2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentane).

questions.q: The colligative property preferred for finding the molar masses of proteins and polymers is ______.
questions.e: Osmotic pressure is large enough to measure even for very dilute solutions and is measured at room temperature, so biomolecules are not damaged.

questions.q: Henry's law states that the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the ______ of the gas above the solution.
questions.e: p = KH × x; this is why soft drink bottles are sealed under high pressure of CO2.

questions.q: What is the van't Hoff factor (i) for NaCl in water, assuming complete dissociation?
questions.e: NaCl → Na+ + Cl-, so one formula unit gives 2 particles, i = 2.

questions.q: 9 g of glucose (molar mass 180 g/mol) is dissolved in 500 g of water. Find the molality of the solution.
questions.e: Moles = 9/180 = 0.05 mol; molality = 0.05/0.5 kg = 0.1 mol/kg.

questions.q: Meera dissolves 1 mol of a non-volatile non-electrolyte in 1 kg of water. For water, Kf = 1.86 K kg/mol and Kb = 0.52 K kg/mol.
p: (a) What is the depression in freezing point?
K
(b) At what temperature does the solution freeze?
°C
(c) What is the elevation in boiling point?
K
questions.e: m = 1 mol/kg, so ΔTf = Kf × m = 1.86 K (freezes at −1.86 °C) and ΔTb = Kb × m = 0.52 K.

questions.q: One faraday is the charge carried by one mole of ______.
questions.e: 1 F = NA × e ≈ 96500 C, the charge of one mole of electrons.

questions.q: Given E°(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V and E°(Zn2+/Zn) = −0.76 V, find the standard emf of the Daniell cell.
questions.e: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V.

questions.q: Aluminium is obtained by electrolysis: Al3+ + 3e- → Al (Al = 27 g/mol, 1 F = 96500 C).
p: (a) How many faradays are needed to deposit 1 mol of Al?
F
(b) How many coulombs is this?
C
(c) What mass of Al is deposited by 1 F of charge?
g
questions.e: Each Al3+ needs 3 electrons, so 3 F = 3 × 96500 = 289500 C per mole; 1 F deposits 27/3 = 9 g of Al.

questions.q: For the Daniell cell, n = 2 and E°cell = 1.1 V. Calculate ΔG° in kJ/mol (F = 96500 C/mol).
A current of 2 A is passed through CuSO4 solution for 965 s. What mass of copper is deposited? (Cu = 63.5 g/mol, F = 96500 C/mol)
The half-life of a reaction of which order is independent of the initial concentration?
questions.e: For a first-order reaction t½ = 0.693/k, which does not depend on [A]0.

questions.q: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.0693 min^-1. Find its half-life.
What fraction of a first-order reactant remains after three half-lives? (Give as a decimal.)
questions.e: After each half-life half remains: (1/2)^3 = 1/8 = 0.125.

questions.q: The extra energy that reactant molecules must absorb, over their average energy, to form products is called ______ energy.
questions.e: Activation energy (Ea) appears in the Arrhenius equation k = A e^(−Ea/RT).

questions.q: The rate law of a reaction is Rate = k[A]^2[B]. If [A] is doubled and [B] is halved, the rate becomes how many times the original?
questions.e: New rate = k(2[A])^2([B]/2) = 4 × 0.5 = 2 times the original.

questions.q: What is the most common oxidation state shown by the lanthanoids?
questions.e: Lanthanoids mainly show the +3 oxidation state; some also show +2 (Eu) or +4 (Ce).

questions.q: Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Mn2+ ion (Z of Mn = 25) in BM.
questions.e: Mn2+ is 3d5 with 5 unpaired electrons; μ = √(n(n+2)) = √35 ≈ 5.92 BM.

questions.q: Zn, Cd and Hg are not regarded as transition elements because they have completely filled ______ orbitals in the ground state and in their common oxidation state.
questions.e: Their configuration is (n−1)d10 ns2 and the M2+ ions are d10, so they lack partly filled d orbitals.

questions.q: An aqueous solution of potassium permanganate (KMnO4) is ______ in colour.
questions.e: The intense purple colour of MnO4- is due to charge transfer, not d–d transitions (Mn is d0).

questions.q: When yellow sodium chromate solution is acidified, it turns ______ due to the formation of dichromate ions.
questions.e: 2CrO4^2- + 2H+ → Cr2O7^2- + H2O; chromate is yellow and dichromate is orange.

questions.q: A ligand that binds to the central metal through two donor atoms, like ethane-1,2-diamine, is called ______.
questions.e: 'en' donates through both nitrogen atoms, so it is bidentate and forms a chelate ring.

questions.q: What is the coordination number of iron in [Fe(CN)6]4-?
questions.e: Six monodentate CN- ligands are attached to Fe, so the coordination number is 6.

questions.q: What is the oxidation state of cobalt in [Co(NH3)6]Cl3?
questions.e: NH3 is neutral and there are three Cl- counter ions, so x + 0 = +3.

questions.q: Choose the correct IUPAC name of K4[Fe(CN)6].
questions.e: Cyanide is named cyanido, an anionic complex takes the -ate ending (ferrate), and Fe is +2 since 4(+1) + x + 6(−1) = 0.

questions.q: Consider the complex tetracarbonylnickel(0), [Ni(CO)4].
p: (a) What is the oxidation state of nickel?
(b) What is the hybridisation of nickel?
sp3
(c) What is the geometry of the complex?
tetrahedral
questions.e: CO is neutral so Ni is 0; strong-field CO pairs up the electrons into 3d10, and the empty 4s and 4p orbitals give sp3 hybridisation and a tetrahedral, diamagnetic complex.

questions.q: The preparation of alkyl iodides by heating alkyl chlorides or bromides with NaI in dry acetone is called the ______ reaction.
questions.e: NaCl or NaBr formed is insoluble in dry acetone and precipitates, driving the Finkelstein reaction forward.

questions.q: An SN2 reaction at a chiral carbon takes place with ______ of configuration.
questions.e: The nucleophile attacks from the side opposite the leaving group, flipping the configuration like an umbrella.

questions.q: Chloroform is slowly oxidised by air in light to a poisonous gas called ______.
questions.e: 2CHCl3 + O2 → 2COCl2 + 2HCl, so chloroform is stored in dark coloured, filled bottles.

questions.q: Which of the following reacts fastest by the SN1 mechanism?
questions.e: SN1 rate depends on carbocation stability; the tertiary carbocation from 2-bromo-2-methylpropane is the most stable.

questions.q: Chlorobenzene is heated with aqueous NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, and the product is then acidified. Name the final product.
questions.e: The C–Cl bond in haloarenes has partial double bond character, so drastic conditions are needed to replace Cl by OH (Dow's process).

questions.q: Wood spirit is the common name of ______.
questions.e: Methanol was originally obtained by destructive distillation of wood, hence the name wood spirit.

questions.q: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because the phenoxide ion is stabilised by ______.
questions.e: The negative charge of phenoxide is delocalised over the benzene ring, while ethoxide's charge stays on oxygen.

questions.q: Phenol treated with chloroform and aqueous NaOH, followed by acidification, gives salicylaldehyde. This is the ______ reaction.
questions.e: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, a –CHO group is introduced at the ortho position of phenol.

questions.q: With Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl2), which class of alcohols gives turbidity immediately at room temperature?
questions.e: Tertiary alcohols form stable carbocations fastest, so the insoluble alkyl chloride separates at once.

questions.q: Ethanol heated with conc. H2SO4 at 413 K gives ethoxyethane. At 443 K the main product is ______.
questions.e: At the higher temperature intramolecular dehydration (elimination) is favoured, giving ethene.

questions.q: Formalin is a 40% aqueous solution of ______.
questions.e: Formalin (about 40% methanal) is used to preserve biological specimens.

questions.q: Aldehydes produce a silver mirror when warmed with ______ reagent.
questions.e: Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) is reduced to metallic silver by aldehydes; most ketones do not react.

questions.q: The only aldehyde that gives a positive iodoform test is ______.
questions.e: The iodoform test needs a CH3CO– group; among aldehydes only ethanal (CH3CHO) has it.

questions.q: Formaldehyde heated with concentrated NaOH gives methanol and ______ (Cannizzaro reaction).
questions.e: Having no α-hydrogen, HCHO undergoes disproportionation: one molecule is reduced to CH3OH and another oxidised to HCOO-Na+.

questions.q: Answer the following about carboxylic acids.
p: (a) Which is the stronger acid: acetic acid or chloroacetic acid?
chloroacetic acid|chloroacetic|chloroethanoic acid|ClCH2COOH
(b) Heating sodium ethanoate with soda lime gives which gas?
methane|CH4
(c) Name the reaction in which a carboxylic acid with α-hydrogen is treated with Cl2 and red phosphorus to give an α-chloro acid.
Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky|HVZ|Hell Volhard Zelinsky
questions.e: The –I effect of Cl stabilises the carboxylate, making ClCH2COOH stronger; decarboxylation of CH3COONa gives CH4; α-halogenation of acids is the HVZ reaction.

questions.q: Primary amines heated with chloroform and ethanolic KOH give foul-smelling isocyanides. This is the ______ test.
questions.e: Only primary amines (aliphatic and aromatic) give the carbylamine test.

questions.q: Hinsberg's reagent, used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines, is ______.
questions.e: Primary amines give an alkali-soluble sulphonamide, secondary give an insoluble one and tertiary do not react.

questions.q: Among methylamine, dimethylamine and trimethylamine, the strongest base in aqueous solution is ______.
questions.e: In water, the combination of +I effect, solvation of the cation and steric factors makes (CH3)2NH the strongest base.

questions.q: Conversion of benzenediazonium chloride into chlorobenzene using CuCl/HCl is called the ______ reaction.
questions.e: In the Sandmeyer reaction, Cu(I) salts replace the –N2+ group by Cl, Br or CN.

questions.q: Ethanamide (CH3CONH2) is treated with Br2 and aqueous NaOH (Hoffmann bromamide degradation). Name the amine formed.
questions.e: The Hoffmann bromamide reaction gives a primary amine with one carbon fewer than the amide, so CH3CONH2 gives CH3NH2.

questions.q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?
questions.e: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid), found in amla and citrus fruits, prevents scurvy (bleeding gums).

questions.q: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives glucose and ______.
questions.e: Sucrose is a disaccharide of α-D-glucose and β-D-fructose; its hydrolysis gives invert sugar.

questions.q: The –CO–NH– bond that links amino acids in proteins is called a ______ bond.
questions.e: A peptide bond forms between the –COOH of one amino acid and the –NH2 of the next with loss of water.

questions.q: Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.e: RNA contains uracil in place of the thymine found in DNA.

questions.q: Glucose is the most abundant monosaccharide.
p: (a) How many carbon atoms does a glucose molecule have?
(b) On prolonged heating with HI, glucose gives which hydrocarbon?
n-hexane|hexane
(c) The bond linking glucose units in maltose and starch is called a ______ linkage.
glycosidic|glycoside|α-glycosidic
questions.e: Formation of n-hexane with HI shows the six carbons are in a straight chain; monosaccharide units are joined by glycosidic (C–O–C) linkages.

questions.q: What is the molar mass of water, H2O (H = 1, O = 16)?
A pure substance made up of only one kind of atom is called an ______.
questions.e: Elements such as oxygen and iron cannot be broken into simpler substances by chemical means.

questions.q: Which scientist gave the law of conservation of mass?
questions.e: Antoine Lavoisier showed that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

questions.q: How many moles are present in 4.4 g of carbon dioxide, CO2 (C = 12, O = 16)?
questions.e: Molar mass of CO2 = 44 g/mol, so moles = 4.4 ÷ 44 = 0.1 mol.

questions.q: What is the mass percentage of carbon in methane, CH4 (C = 12, H = 1)?
questions.e: Molar mass = 16 g/mol, so % C = 12 ÷ 16 × 100 = 75%.

questions.q: Molarity is the number of moles of solute in one ______ of solution.
questions.e: Molarity M = moles of solute ÷ volume of solution in litres.

questions.q: Molality is the number of moles of solute per kilogram of ______.
questions.e: Molality does not change with temperature because it uses mass, not volume.

questions.q: How many grams of NaOH (molar mass 40 g/mol) are needed to make 500 mL of a 0.2 M solution?
questions.e: Moles = 0.2 × 0.5 = 0.1 mol, and mass = 0.1 × 40 = 4 g.

questions.q: What is the empirical formula of benzene, C6H6?
questions.e: The simplest whole-number ratio of C to H in C6H6 is 1 : 1.

questions.q: A compound has the empirical formula CH2O and a molar mass of 180 g/mol. What is its molecular formula?
questions.e: The empirical formula mass is 30, and 180 ÷ 30 = 6, so the formula is (CH2O)6 = C6H12O6.

questions.q: 2 g of hydrogen gas reacts with 32 g of oxygen gas: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O (H = 1, O = 16).
p: (a) Which reactant is the limiting reagent?
hydrogen|H2
(b) What mass of water is formed?
g
(c) How many moles of oxygen are left over?
mol
questions.e: There is 1 mol of H2 and 1 mol of O2. 1 mol of H2 needs only 0.5 mol of O2, so hydrogen is limiting; it gives 1 mol (18 g) of water and 0.5 mol of O2 is left.

questions.q: Electrons were discovered through experiments on ______ rays.
questions.e: J. J. Thomson measured the charge-to-mass ratio of cathode-ray particles (electrons).

questions.q: Which quantum number describes the shape of an orbital?
questions.e: The azimuthal quantum number l gives the subshell (s, p, d, f) and the shape of the orbital.

questions.q: What is the shape of an s orbital?
questions.e: An s orbital is spherically symmetrical about the nucleus.

questions.q: By the Pauli exclusion principle, no two electrons in an atom can have the same set of four ______ numbers.
questions.e: So an orbital can hold at most two electrons, with opposite spins.

questions.q: By Hund's rule, electrons in orbitals of the same subshell do not pair up until each orbital is ______ occupied.
questions.e: For example, nitrogen has three unpaired electrons in its three 2p orbitals.

questions.q: What is the largest number of electrons that one orbital can hold?
questions.e: The two electrons in an orbital have opposite spins.

questions.q: By the aufbau principle, which subshell is filled immediately after 3p?
questions.e: By the (n + l) rule, 4s (4 + 0 = 4) is lower in energy than 3d (3 + 2 = 5).

questions.q: Chromium (Z = 24) has the configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s1. How many unpaired electrons does it have?
questions.e: Five in the 3d orbitals and one in 4s: a half-filled d subshell is extra stable.

questions.q: What is the value of the azimuthal quantum number l for a 3d orbital?
questions.e: l = 0, 1, 2, 3 for s, p, d, f.

questions.q: Consider the shell with n = 4.
p: (a) What is the largest number of electrons it can hold?
(b) How many subshells does it have?
(c) How many orbitals does it have?
questions.e: Electrons = 2n^2 = 32; subshells 4s, 4p, 4d and 4f; orbitals = n^2 = 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The elements of group 18 are called ______ gases.
questions.e: Helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon have completely filled valence shells.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The elements of group 1 (except hydrogen) are called ______ metals.
questions.e: Lithium, sodium and potassium form strongly alkaline hydroxides.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The halogens belong to which group of the periodic table?
questions.e: Fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine are in group 17.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The energy needed to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom in its ground state is called ______ enthalpy.
questions.e: It is measured in kJ/mol.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: On going down a group, the atomic radius generally ______.
questions.e: A new shell is added at each step down a group.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The f-block elements are also called ______ transition elements.
questions.e: They are the lanthanoids and actinoids.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which period of the periodic table has only 2 elements?
questions.e: The first period has only hydrogen and helium.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Elements in the same group have the same number of ______ electrons.
questions.e: This is why elements in a group have similar chemical properties.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which is larger: a sodium atom (Na) or a sodium ion (Na+)?
questions.e: Na+ has lost its outer 3s electron and its shell, so it is much smaller than the Na atom.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Nitrogen has a higher first ionisation enthalpy than oxygen because nitrogen has an extra-stable ______-filled 2p subshell.
questions.e: Oxygen (2p4) loses its paired electron more easily than nitrogen (2p3) loses one from a half-filled subshell.

questions.t: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: An element has atomic number 20.
p: (a) In which period is it?
(b) In which group is it?
(c) In which block is it? Answer s, p, d or f.
s|s-block|s block
questions.e: The configuration is [Ar] 4s2: period 4, group 2, s-block. The element is calcium.

questions.q: A bond formed by the complete transfer of electrons from one atom to another is called an ______ bond.
questions.e: NaCl is held together by ionic bonds between Na+ and Cl- ions.

questions.q: By the octet rule, atoms tend to gain, lose or share electrons to have how many electrons in their outermost shell?
questions.e: Eight valence electrons give a noble gas configuration.

questions.q: What is the shape of a carbon dioxide (CO2) molecule?
questions.e: The two C=O bonds are at 180°, so CO2 is linear and non-polar.

questions.q: By VSEPR theory, what is the shape of the ammonia (NH3) molecule?
questions.e: Three bond pairs and one lone pair around nitrogen give a pyramidal shape.

questions.q: What is the hybridisation of boron in BF3?
questions.e: Boron forms three bonds and has no lone pair, giving trigonal planar sp2 hybridisation.

questions.q: How many lone pairs of electrons are there on the oxygen atom in a water molecule?
questions.e: Oxygen has two bond pairs and two lone pairs, which makes the molecule bent.

questions.q: Hydrogen bonding between water molecules explains why water has an unusually high ______ point.
questions.e: Extra energy is needed to break the hydrogen bonds, so water boils at 100 °C although H2S is a gas.

questions.q: What is the bond order of the N2 molecule according to molecular orbital theory?
questions.e: Bond order = ½(bonding − antibonding electrons) = ½(10 − 4) = 3, a triple bond.

questions.q: Which bond is more polar, H–F or H–Cl?
questions.e: Fluorine is more electronegative than chlorine, so the H–F bond is more polar.

questions.q: Consider the SF6 molecule.
p: (a) What is the hybridisation of sulphur?
sp3d2
(b) What is the shape of the molecule?
octahedral|octahedron
questions.e: Sulphur forms six bonds with no lone pair, using sp3d2 hybrid orbitals directed to the corners of an octahedron.

questions.q: A system that can exchange energy but not matter with its surroundings is called a ______ system.
questions.e: A sealed metal container of gas is a closed system.

questions.q: For a reaction that releases heat (an exothermic reaction), ΔH is ______.
questions.e: Heat leaves the system, so its enthalpy decreases.

questions.q: The enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states is the standard enthalpy of ______.
questions.e: It is written ΔfH°.

questions.q: What is the standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its standard state?
questions.e: By convention, ΔfH° of O2(g), C(graphite) and similar elements is zero.

questions.q: By Hess's law, the total enthalpy change of a reaction is the same whether it happens in one step or in ______ steps.
questions.e: Enthalpy is a state function, so it depends only on the initial and final states.

questions.q: Entropy is a measure of the ______ of a system.
questions.e: Gases have more entropy than liquids, and liquids more than solids.

questions.q: For a spontaneous process at constant temperature and pressure, ΔG is ______.
questions.e: ΔG < 0 means the process can happen on its own.

questions.q: ΔH = ΔU + Δn(g)RT. For a reaction in which Δn(g) = 0, ΔH equals ______.
questions.e: If the number of moles of gas does not change, ΔH and ΔU are equal, as in H2(g) + Cl2(g) → 2HCl(g).

questions.q: Calculate ΔG at 300 K for a reaction with ΔH = −20 kJ/mol and ΔS = −50 J/K/mol.
C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g); ΔH = −393.5 kJ/mol. How much heat is released when 2 mol of carbon burn completely?
A reaction has ΔH = +40 kJ/mol and ΔS = +100 J/K/mol.
p: (a) What is ΔG at 300 K?
kJ/mol
(b) Above what temperature does the reaction become spontaneous?
K
questions.e: ΔG = 40 − 300 × 0.1 = +10 kJ/mol, so it is not spontaneous at 300 K. ΔG = 0 when T = ΔH ÷ ΔS = 40 000 ÷ 100 = 400 K.

questions.q: At equilibrium, the rates of the forward and backward reactions are ______.
questions.e: Equilibrium is dynamic: both reactions continue at the same rate.

questions.q: A substance like water that can act both as an acid and as a base is called ______.
questions.e: Water can donate a proton (to NH3) or accept one (from HCl).

questions.q: According to Arrhenius, an acid produces ______ ions in water.
questions.e: A base produces hydroxide ions in water.

questions.q: What is the pH of a solution with [H+] = 10^-4 M?
questions.e: pH = −log[H+] = 4.

questions.q: At 298 K, what is pH + pOH for any aqueous solution?
A Lewis acid is an electron-pair ______.
questions.e: BF3 is a Lewis acid; NH3, which donates a lone pair, is a Lewis base.

questions.q: Increasing the pressure on N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) shifts the equilibrium towards the side with ______ moles of gas.
questions.e: There are 4 moles of gas on the left and 2 on the right, so more ammonia forms.

questions.q: A solution that resists a change in pH when a small amount of acid or base is added is called a ______ solution.
questions.e: A mixture of acetic acid and sodium acetate is a buffer.

questions.q: For the reaction A ⇌ B, Kc = 4. What is Kc for the reverse reaction B ⇌ A?
questions.e: The equilibrium constant of the reverse reaction is 1 ÷ Kc = 1/4.

questions.q: A 0.1 M solution of acetic acid is 1% ionised.
p: (a) What is the hydrogen ion concentration?
M
(b) What is the pH?

questions.q: In terms of electron transfer, reduction is the ______ of electrons.
questions.e: OIL RIG: oxidation is loss, reduction is gain.

questions.q: A substance that is itself reduced and oxidises another substance is called an ______ agent.
questions.e: KMnO4 and K2Cr2O7 are common oxidising agents.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of an element in its free, uncombined state?
questions.e: In H2, O2, Na or Fe, each atom has oxidation number zero.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of oxygen in hydrogen peroxide, H2O2?
questions.e: 2(+1) + 2x = 0, so x = −1. Peroxides are an exception to the usual −2.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of sulphur in H2SO4?
What is the oxidation number of nitrogen in ammonia, NH3?
In the reaction Zn + Cu2+ → Zn2+ + Cu, which species is oxidised?
questions.e: Zinc loses two electrons and its oxidation number rises from 0 to +2.

questions.q: A reaction in which the same element is both oxidised and reduced is called a ______ reaction.
questions.e: For example, 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of carbon in CO2?
In 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2, oxygen changes from −1 to −2 in water, and to what oxidation number in O2?
questions.e: Oxygen in O2 has oxidation number 0, so some oxygen is oxidised (−1 → 0) and some reduced (−1 → −2).

questions.q: In acidic solution, dichromate ions (Cr2O7^2-) oxidise Fe2+ ions to Fe3+, and are themselves reduced to Cr3+.
p: (a) By how much does the oxidation number of each chromium atom change?
(b) How many moles of Fe2+ are oxidised by 1 mol of Cr2O7^2-?
mol
questions.e: Each Cr goes from +6 to +3, gaining 3 electrons, so one Cr2O7^2- gains 6 electrons, enough to oxidise 6 Fe2+ ions.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH3COCH3?
questions.e: It has three carbon atoms and a ketone group; its common name is acetone.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: The –CHO functional group is present in ______.
questions.e: Methanal (HCHO) and ethanal (CH3CHO) are aldehydes.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: Which technique separates the components of a mixture by their different adsorption, for example the pigments in a leaf extract?
questions.e: The components move at different rates over a stationary phase.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH3CH2CH2CHO?
questions.e: Four carbon atoms including the –CHO carbon: butanal.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: A species in which a carbon atom carries a negative charge is called a ______.
questions.e: A carbocation has a positively charged carbon; a free radical has an unpaired electron.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: When a covalent bond breaks so that each atom keeps one electron of the shared pair (homolytic cleavage), the products are ______.
questions.e: Heterolytic cleavage, by contrast, gives ions.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: In the test for halogens, the sodium fusion extract gives a white precipitate with silver nitrate. Which halogen is present?
questions.e: AgCl is white and soluble in ammonia; AgBr is pale yellow and AgI is yellow.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: Which is more stable, a tertiary carbocation or a primary carbocation?
questions.e: Alkyl groups release electrons (by inductive effect and hyperconjugation) and spread the positive charge.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: Nucleophiles are electron-______ species.
questions.e: Nucleophiles such as OH- and NH3 donate an electron pair to an electron-deficient centre.

questions.t: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.q: Consider the compound CH3CH(OH)CH3.
p: (a) What is its IUPAC name?
propan-2-ol|2-propanol|propan 2 ol
(b) Which class of compounds does it belong to?
alcohol|alcohols|secondary alcohol
questions.e: The –OH group is on the second of three carbon atoms, so it is propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol.

questions.q: Alkanes are called ______ hydrocarbons because they contain only single bonds.
questions.e: Every carbon atom in an alkane is joined to four other atoms by single bonds.

questions.q: What is the general formula of alkenes?
questions.e: Ethene is C2H4 and propene is C3H6.

questions.q: What is the molecular formula of benzene?
questions.e: Benzene is a planar ring of six carbon atoms.

questions.q: Adding hydrogen to an alkene in the presence of a nickel catalyst gives an ______.
questions.e: For example, CH2=CH2 + H2 → CH3–CH3.

questions.q: In the Wurtz reaction, alkyl halides react with sodium in dry ether to give ______.
questions.e: 2CH3Br + 2Na → CH3–CH3 + 2NaBr.

questions.q: In the presence of a peroxide, HBr adds to propene to give 1-bromopropane. This anti-Markovnikov addition is called the peroxide or ______ effect.
questions.e: It goes by a free-radical mechanism; the effect is seen only with HBr.

questions.q: Ethene decolourises bromine water. This shows that ethene has a carbon–carbon ______ bond.
questions.e: Bromine adds across the double bond to give 1,2-dibromoethane.

questions.q: What is the hybridisation of each carbon atom in benzene?
questions.e: Each carbon forms three σ bonds in a plane; the unhybridised p orbitals form the π electron cloud.

questions.q: How many structural isomers are possible for C4H10?
questions.e: Butane and 2-methylpropane.

questions.q: Because of its stable π electron cloud, benzene mainly undergoes ______ substitution reactions.
questions.e: Nitration, halogenation and Friedel–Crafts reactions are electrophilic substitutions.

questions.q: By Hückel's rule, a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated compound is aromatic if it has (4n + 2) π electrons.
p: (a) What is the value of n for benzene?
(b) How many π electrons does the rule require when n = 2?
questions.e: Benzene has 6 π electrons: 4n + 2 = 6 gives n = 1. For n = 2, 4 × 2 + 2 = 10.
